messages:
Alex K: Ran an nsys capture on the nightly stack after the batching heuristic tweak. Seeing higher all-reduce overlap and strange KV-cache evictions. cc @Priya S :eyes:
Priya S: Can you drop the nsys command you used and the commit SHA?
Alex K: sha: 5f3a2b1. Command: `nsys profile --output trace_nightly --sample=none --capture-range=nvtx` then perfetto -> converted to .pftrace.
Ben W: Any difference between multi-GPU and single-GPU runs?
Alex K: Single-GPU looks fine. Multi-GPU (4x A100) shows more cross-GPU idle time during token generation.
Maria L: Uploading perfetto slice (.pftrace) to the traces bucket: gs://rwinf-traces/1777777777/perfetto_pftrace.pftrace :link:
Sam T: Quick hypothesis: the new batching groups small requests to hit larger batch size which inflates sequence padding -> longer collective windows. Could increase all-reduce contribution.
Priya S: Do we have KV cache handshake timings? I remember a previous regression where the prefetcher would flush entries when batches changed shape.
Alex K: Good call. From the trace (grep-like summary):
```
KVHandshake: 12us -> 1.1ms spikes across ranks
KVCacheRetire: frequent at response boundaries (~8-12ms)
AllReduce windows: mean 2.4ms -> tail 27ms
CUDA kernels: small-kernel count up ~58% higher
```
Ben W: That 1.1ms spike on handshake is worrying. Could be serialization when we rebind caches between varied batch shapes. Any NVTX markers around those times?
Alex K: Yes NVTX: `kv:recv_handshake` then `dp:model_forward` then `nccl:allreduce_start`. The order repeats per micro-batch when padding changed.
Maria L: I flashed a zoomed perfetto screenshot — the timeline shows back-to-back small kernels, then a big NCCL allreduce tail, then idle. Looks like we aren't overlapping communication and compute effectively.
Sam T: Do we still use the async kernel selector path for those cases? The change earlier toggled selector to 'aggressive' for sub-batch fusion. Might cause different launch ordering.
Priya S: If selector changes launch order, the NCCL enqueue pattern might serialize collectives. Need to see kernel stream assignment.
Alex K: Here's a small snippet from the converted nsight timeline (trimmed):
```
stream 1: kernel A (0.3ms) -> kernel B (0.2ms) -> cudaMemcpyAsync -> ncclAllReduce
stream 2: kernel C (0.1ms) -> kv:retire -> nvtx sync -> ncclAllReduce
```
Ben W: That nvtx sync flag suggests we force a host-side sync before the collective. Where in the code do we set NVTX markers around KV retire?
Priya S: It's in kv_manager.cpp: `NVTX_RANGE_PUSH("kv:retire_sync"); cudaStreamSynchronize(prefetch_stream);` — oof. That was a defensive sync to avoid stale pointers.
Maria L: If batching now causes prefetch_stream activity to be interleaved, that sync will block other compute streams and delay NCCL progression.
Sam T: Possible fixes: 1) remove sync and ensure memory ordering via events, 2) move prefetch to a dedicated non-blocking stream and use cudaEventRecord/cudaStreamWaitEvent, 3) change batching to preserve per-request stream affinity.
Alex K: I prototyped (2) locally: replaced cudaStreamSynchronize with event-based wait. Re-ran nsys; all-reduce tail dropped from 27ms -> 6ms, KV handshake stable ~40us.
Ben W: Nice. Any regression on P50 latency?
Alex K: P50 slightly improved (~3%); P99 improved more (~18%). Cost per token unchanged.
Priya S: Can you push the prototype to a feature branch and tag QA? Need perf runs across 8x A100 and TP=2 config.
Alex K: Pushing branch `kv-event-prefetch-1777`. Run matrix requested: 4xA100 TP=1, 4xA100 TP=2, 8xA100 TP=4.
Maria L: Also add an nsys perfetto capture with NCCL_TRACE env on for one run so we can correlate NVTX->NCCL.
Sam T: Keep an eye on kernel selector flags. If aggressive fusion reduces kernel count but increases shape variance, event-based solution still better than sync.
Ben W: Could also be worth adding a micro-benchmark that toggles padding strategy and measures all-reduce occupancy.
Priya S: I can write that micro-benchmark. Will run it tomorrow morning and post results.
Alex K: For completeness, here's the minimal repro command I used to trigger the issue:
```
RUNTIME_FLAGS="--batching=aggressive --kv_prefetch=on" ./run_inference.sh --model rwinf/llama-7b --seq 1024 --concurrency 64
nsys profile --output out.nsys --trace=nvtx,cuda,nvtx
```
Maria L: Thanks. If QA passes, we should roll this event-based change into a canary for dedicated clusters. Add a metric to track KV handshake mean in console dashboards.
Ben W: Agreed. Also add an alert when all-reduce tail > 10ms for >1% of requests.
Priya S: I'll draft the PR description explaining the sync -> event swap and include before/after nsight screenshots + perf numbers.
Alex K: Uploaded diff and perf numbers at gs://rwinf-traces/1777777777/kv-event-diff.txt. Moving to test grid now. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: CI pipeline queued: build-1777-kv-event (gpu/e2e) — status: queued
Sam T: Great detective work team. If micro-benchmarks show no regressions, this looks like the right mitigation.
Alex K: Closing loop after QA results. Thanks all.
